response.markdown_report:
The recommended first experiment is **attribute-preserving text fusion within HSTU**, targeting overly broad matches and compatibility mismatches while testing whether finer item representations improve Electronics separation. This is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated improvement.

### Insights and framework

Three starting-point insights guide selection. First, useful recommendations extend a specific recent purpose. Broad historical similarity therefore provides an incomplete learning signal. Second, compatibility mismatches recur in user feedback. Available titles and descriptions may expose connectors, dimensions and formats, but missing specifications remain unknown. Third, Electronics has a 10.71% sampled wrong-rank rate and a −0.0749 tenth-percentile margin. Embedding scores near 0.5 provide little evidence of directional collapse, so collapse regularization lacks diagnostic support.

Three literature insights suggest constrained adaptations. HSTU already supplies gated sequential processing [1]. Keeping that backbone permits a focused representation experiment. HSTU-BLaIR adds text representations to item IDs [2]. Its pretrained encoder prevents directly transferring its effectiveness claim to this setting. MARS motivates preserving attribute-level distinctions [3]. Its pretrained components similarly leave scratch-trained effectiveness unresolved.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Gap and proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal intent | HSTU; TLSRec [4] | Recent-purpose gating; fulfilled needs remain unobserved |
| Item specificity | HSTU-BLaIR; MARS | Train title/description fusion from scratch |
| Ranking supervision | Sampled-softmax analysis [5] | Test moderate hard negatives against easy-negative saturation |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Text fusion: 5/8/9/7/5.** Originality: practical constrained adaptation, but established fusion pattern. Potential: reusable specificity features, but sparse metadata limits coverage. User alignment: targets broad matches and compatibility, but cannot verify missing specifications. Model alignment: may separate confusing Electronics items, but evidence is indirect. Difficulty: compact shared encoder, but requires metadata and predictor parity.
- **Recent-history gate: 4/7/7/5/4.** Originality: focused temporal adaptation, but familiar gating. Potential: transferable intent modeling, but sparse sequences weaken estimates. User alignment: addresses stale associations and potentially redundancy, but completed needs are unlabeled. Model alignment: may reduce contextual confusion, but lacks direct diagnostic evidence. Difficulty: small module, but causal alignment needs care.
- **Moderate hard-negative curriculum: 3/7/5/9/3.** Originality: straightforward objective change, but well established. Potential: efficient ranking improvement, but false negatives persist. User alignment: distinguishes alternatives, but supplies no compatibility evidence. Model alignment: directly targets weak margins, but training margins can mislead. Difficulty: modest sampler changes, but mining adds cost.

### Selected experiment

At 0% progress, begin with text fusion alone. Preserve numbers, units, model identifiers and format tokens; train a small shared token encoder from scratch. Fuse its output with item IDs before the unchanged HSTU backbone and reuse that representation for candidate scoring. This addresses broad thematic substitution and compatibility mismatches; improved Electronics margins are the model-facing hypothesis.

```text
item(i) = ID(i) + projection(masked_mean(token_embeddings(text(i))))
features = HSTU(item(left_padded_history))
score(i) = dot(features[final_nonpadding_position], item(i))
```

Keep baseline loss and sampling initially. Select exclusively by fixed macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint/category, all routing, prescribed seeds and training limits. Embed identical architecture and vocabulary in the predictor writer, and preserve diagnostic interfaces.

idea.description: Train one HSTU per category with jointly learned, attribute-preserving title/description embeddings fused into item-ID representations. Use the same fused item representation for sequence inputs and candidate scoring.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad thematic substitution and practical compatibility mismatches. Electronics also exhibits the weakest sampled separation: a 10.71% wrong-rank rate and −0.0749 tenth-percentile margin. Text fusion could expose distinctions absent from item IDs, although compatibility and validation gains remain experimental.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep the supplied corrected HSTU backbone, baseline objective and sampler for the first isolated experiment. Build vocabulary only from permitted supplied titles/descriptions; preserve numbers, units, connectors and format identifiers. Use a small randomly initialized token embedding table, masked mean pooling and a learned projection; missing text contributes zero. Cache token IDs, not detached learned representations. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items); adapt probes so effective candidate scores use the fused representation while any raw-ID embedding statistic is explicitly labeled. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics with definitions. Do not interpret unavailable category breakdowns or metadata as evidence. For left-padded histories, gather the greatest nonzero sequence index, never count minus one; handle empty histories explicitly. Serialize vocabulary, token tables, architecture configuration and weights with each category checkpoint, and update the embedded predictor writer identically. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and the fixed evaluator. Use one independently trained checkpoint per category without fusion across models. No training or validation result is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each of the four categories:
  Initialize the corrected HSTU and a small text encoder using seed 42.
  Tokenize permitted item titles/descriptions, preserving attribute-bearing tokens.
  Define item_repr(ids):
    text = masked_mean(token_embedding(token_ids[ids]))
    return item_emb(ids) + text_projection(text), with padding forced to zero
  Define log2feats(sequence):
    return existing_HSTU_backbone(item_repr(sequence), existing_causal_masks)
  Define predict_score(features, items):
    return dot(features, item_repr(items))
  Train with unchanged baseline targets, loss and sampling within prescribed limits.
  For sequence-level prediction, gather the final nonpadding feature.
  Evaluate through the fixed validation protocol and preserve diagnostic contracts.
  Save one selected checkpoint and matching predictor configuration/vocabulary.
Select the experiment using four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Adapts attribute-preserving text fusion to a scratch-trained, single-model HSTU experiment under a tightly controlled benchmark.
originality.negative: ID-plus-text fusion is established; the contribution is a constrained adaptation rather than a new backbone.

future_potential.positive: A shared item representation could support increasingly precise task, format and compatibility distinctions using permitted metadata.
future_potential.negative: Sparse descriptions and the absence of explicit compatibility or fulfilled-need labels limit what the network can learn.

code_difficulty.positive: The encoder and fusion are small additions that preserve the HSTU sequence backbone and allow an isolated first experiment.
code_difficulty.negative: Metadata alignment, padding behavior, effective-score diagnostics and checkpoint/predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with pointwise attention, relative biases and multiplicative gating.
Provides the backbone retained by the proposed experiment.
limitations: Does not establish explicit detection of fulfilled needs or practical compatibility.
Does not establish gains for the supplied pinned Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Adds projected text embeddings to trainable item-ID embeddings before HSTU.
Provides the closest architectural motivation for the selected fusion experiment.
limitations: Uses a frozen pretrained BLaIR encoder, which is unavailable under this task's constraints.
Its results do not establish effectiveness for a text encoder trained from scratch.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: Uses attribute-aware text representations and attribute-wise user–item matching.
Motivates retaining fine item distinctions that pooled broad similarity can obscure.
limitations: Does not demonstrate compatibility inference or gains for this constrained HSTU experiment.

related_work.title: TLSRec
contributions: Models local and global preferences with a dimension-wise gate conditioned on elapsed time.
limitations: Temporal gating does not supply labels for fulfilled needs.
Reported findings do not establish improvements under the pinned evaluation.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: Analyzes how sampled-softmax training emphasizes informative negatives and how temperature affects gradient concentration.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal negative sampler or temperature for these four categories.
Strong sampled training margins do not guarantee held-out HR@10.
